title: ccw-classic-1996-world-heavyweight
label: Desmond Harrison

won.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (3m9r_eoKeP0J, 25 March 1997): an 8-man single-elimination tournament on 30 March 1997 "to crown the FIRST ever CCW WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT CHAMPION", Desmond Harrison among the eight. The tournament's own results do not survive; the fed's own later documents name him its first champion (RSPWF-debut promo YIse7-DWHNUJ: "former CCW World Champion Desmond Harrison"; the 2001 card 9CRcNZaARBgJ: "the man who first held the CCW World Title").

how: Won the 8-man single-elimination tournament the fed's own "Explosion!!" pay-per-view staged to crown its first World Heavyweight Champion, 30 March 1997.
note: Lost the title to X.Plosion at CCW FanFest (Harrison: "Kain may have helped you take the title at FanFest"); challenged for it again in the main event of Slamfest, 9 July 1997, and lost to the Mushroom Cloud.

lost.source: Lost to X.Plosion at CCW FanFest, a show whose own card does not survive; it falls after Explosion!! (30 March 1997) and before the RSPWF-debut promo of 7 July 1997, which already bills X.Plosion "the current champion".

title: ccw-classic-1996-international
label: "Boardwalk" Bradley Warden

won.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (3m9r_eoKeP0J, 25 March 1997), a recap clip: "Bradley Warden pinning Ricky Revolution to become the first ever CCW InterNational Champion." No dated document of the win survives; it falls between the fed's first card, First Night (18 January 1997), and the promo that recaps it.

how: Pinned Ricky Revolution to become the first CCW International Champion.
note: Billed to defend the title against Ricky Revolution at Explosion!! (30 March 1997), a No Holds Brawled match Slamfest's commentary recalls; its result does not survive. The same promo's recap footage shows him pinning X.Plosion, a win Slamfest's commentary also recalls.

lost.source: Lost the title to Ricky Revolution (Slamfest, 9 July 1997: Revolution "_FORMER_ CCW International Champion"; Warden "recapture this gold from another superstar, Ricky Revolution"). The Explosion!! promo of 25 March 1997 still has Warden holding the gold; no surviving document records the night or the match.

title: ccw-classic-1996-west-coast
label: "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz

won.source: The fed's own RSPWF-debut promo (YIse7-DWHNUJ): "the former CCW West Coast Champion 'GQ' Geoffrey Quartz, just after he won the title at First Night" (First Night self-dated 18 January 1997). Corroborated by the fed's own "First Night" card announcement (r4zfr6TQsp4J, 18 Dec 1996), which bills Geoffrey Quartz in Round One of the four-man West Coast Championship tournament this show crowned.

how: Won the four-man West Coast Championship tournament at CCW's own "First Night" debut show, 18 January 1997, pinning Ricky Revolution for the title.
note: Billed to defend the title against Bill MacRagge at Explosion!! (30 March 1997); that result does not survive. Lost it to his brother Ian at FanFest after more than a minute in the Equation deathlock, and was out injured with his back on Slamfest, 9 July 1997.

lost.source: Lost to his brother Ian Quartz at CCW FanFest, submitting to the Equation deathlock (Slamfest of 9 July 1997, jpNricY9dGYJ, "exclusive footage from CCW FanFest"). FanFest's own card does not survive; it falls after Explosion!! (30 March 1997), where he was billed to defend the title, and before the RSPWF-debut promo of 7 July 1997 (YIse7-DWHNUJ), which calls him "the former CCW West Coast Champion".

title: ccw-classic-1996-west-coast
label: "IQ" Ian Quartz

won.source: The fed's own Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ): "exclusive footage from CCW FanFest" of Ian Quartz locking his brother GQ in the Equation deathlock "en route to a title win", GQ "finally submitting"; Mark Frost calls him "newly crowned". FanFest's own card does not survive; it falls after Explosion!! (30 March 1997) and before the RSPWF-debut promo of 7 July 1997 (YIse7-DWHNUJ), which already calls GQ "the former CCW West Coast Champion".

how: Beat his brother, "GQ" Geoffrey Quartz, for the title at CCW FanFest, by submission to the Equation deathlock.
note: Won a future title shot for Ricky Revolution by losing a non-title match to him on 9 July 1997; the shot itself is not resolved in this corpus.

title: ccw-classic-1996-world-heavyweight
label: X.Plosion

won.source: The fed's own Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ): X.Plosion, "my match with Harrison at FanFest ... the LAST CCW world title change"; Harrison, "Kain may have helped you take the title at FanFest". FanFest's own card does not survive; it falls after Explosion!! (30 March 1997) and before the RSPWF-debut promo of 7 July 1997 (YIse7-DWHNUJ), which already bills him "the current champion".

how: Beat Desmond Harrison for the title at CCW FanFest (by Harrison's account, with his bodyguard Kain's help).
note: Retained against Desmond Harrison in the main event of Slamfest, 9 July 1997, the fed's RSPWF debut; still champion when the fed's 1997 record breaks off.

title: ccw-classic-1996-international
label: "The Bullet" Ricky Revolution

won.source: The fed's own Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ): Robert Flamingo introduces him as "_FORMER_ CCW International Champion" and asks about "losing the International Title"; Stevie West: "Ricky is the lightest champion in CCW history, but that sure as hell didn't stop him from taking the gold!"; Bradley Warden: "recapture this gold from another superstar, Ricky Revolution". The Explosion!! promo of 25 March 1997 (3m9r_eoKeP0J) still has Warden holding the gold. No surviving document records the night or the match.

how: Took the title from Bradley Warden; the night and the match are not recorded.

lost.source: Lost it back to Bradley Warden (Slamfest, 9 July 1997: Revolution, "I lost, cause I got bored with facing Warden and the only way he'd shut up was to let him win"; Fast Fighter, Warden "has finally finished off his feud with Ricky and gotten his International Title back").

note: Slamfest's Classic Cup segment shows Warden's figure-four on him at FanFest; no surviving document says on which night the title changed hands either way.

title: ccw-classic-1996-international
label: "Boardwalk" Bradley Warden

won.source: The fed's own Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ): Fast Fighter, Warden "has finally finished off his feud with Ricky and gotten his International Title back"; Warden, "allowed me to recapture this gold from another superstar, Ricky Revolution"; Robert Flamingo bills him "2-Time CCW International Champion". No surviving document records the night.

how: Won the title back from Ricky Revolution.
note: Champion on Slamfest, 9 July 1997, the fed's RSPWF debut, where he beat Bill MacRagge in a non-title match; still champion when the fed's 1997 record breaks off.

title: ccw-classic-1996-world-tag-team
label: Murder Inc.

won.source: The fed's own "Explosion!!" PPV promo (3m9r_eoKeP0J, 25 March 1997): footage of Murder Inc. "beating the Devestation Express to become the first ever tag team champions"; "now that Murder Inc. hold the coveted tag straps". No dated document of the win survives; it falls between the fed's first card, First Night (18 January 1997), and the promo.

how: Beat the Devestation Express to become the fed's first tag team champions.

lost.source: By Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ) Fire & Ice are "the CCW Tag Team Champions". No surviving document records when Murder Inc. lost the titles, or to whom.

note: Billed to defend the titles against Fire & Ice at Explosion!! (30 March 1997); that result does not survive.

title: ccw-classic-1996-world-tag-team
label: Fire & Ice

won.source: The fed's own Slamfest of 9 July 1997 (jpNricY9dGYJ): "Michael Ice of the CCW Tag Team Champions, Fire & Ice"; Ellis King, "Fire & Ice, we know who's got the gold". The Explosion!! promo of 25 March 1997 (3m9r_eoKeP0J) still has Murder Inc. holding the titles. The fed's own card of 1 February 2001 (/promotions/ccw-classic-1996/archive/ccw-classic-thursday-night-slam-2001-02-08.html) names the team's two men, "Iceman" Michael Ice and "Red Hot" Alex Perkins, and says "This team was the last CCW Tag Team Champions before we closed doors".

how: Held the titles by the fed's first RSPWF broadcast; the title change is not recorded.
note: Champions on Slamfest, 9 July 1997; the fed's own 2001 cards call Fire & Ice the last CCW Tag Team Champions, and its update of 7 February 2001 lists the CCW Tag Team Title vacant.
